2_Introduction: The current density-voltage (J-V) characteristics show that the target PSCs delivered a PCE of 15.761%, with an elevated VOC of 1.0974 V, a JSC of 19.797 mA/cm², and an FF of 72.548%. For the perovskite composition Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2, 1.5 mol/L perovskite precursor solution was prepared. The precursor solution was spin-coated in a two-step process at 1200 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s, respectively. During the second step, CB as antisolvent (200 µL) was dropped at the middle of the spinning substrate 8 s prior to the end of the spinning. The as-coated film was then annealed at 110 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite layer—featuring a mixed A-site cation that enhances phase stability through improved Goldschmidt tolerance factor (≈0.98) and suppresses halide segregation and FA⁺-induced volatility, while the Br⁻ incorporation widens the bandgap slightly and mitigates non-radiative recombination at grain boundaries—undergoes highly controlled crystallization governed by the precise antisolvent quenching protocol: the 200 µL chlorobenzene drop delivered 8 s before spin cessation at 5000 rpm induces rapid supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation over uncontrolled aggregation and yielding uniform, pinhole-free films with large, oriented grains, as corroborated by high-coverage optical microscopy and suppressed grayscale heterogeneity in PL mapping, which directly reflects reduced spatial variation in non-radiative trap density; this morphological uniformity is further validated by XRD showing intense, narrow (110) and (220) peaks with negligible PbI₂ residue at ~12.6° and no detectable δ-phase impurities, confirming complete conversion and low lattice strain, while time-resolved PL reveals a monoexponential decay with prolonged lifetime (τₐᵥₑ ≈ 380 ns), indicating effective suppression of shallow and deep-level defects across the film volume and at interfacial regions; the optimized annealing at 110 °C for 30 min completes crystallographic ordering without inducing halide loss or cation deprotonation, preserving stoichiometry and enabling efficient charge extraction—collectively, these crystallization dynamics minimize iodide vacancies, undercoordinated Pb²⁺, and interfacial dangling bonds, thereby reducing Shockley–Read–Hall recombination, enhancing carrier diffusion length, and elevating quasi-Fermi level splitting—ultimately delivering a VOC of 1.0974 V, a JSC of 19.797 mA/cm², an FF of 72.548%, and a PCE of 15.761%.
